qs.q: A child with a history of recurrent urinary tract infections and vesicoureteric reflux is found to have renal scarring. Which imaging modality is considered the gold standard for diagnosing renal scarring?
qs.e: Radionuclide DMSA scans are identified as the gold standard for detecting renal scarring due to their high sensitivity. Ultrasound has poor sensitivity for scarring, and VCU is primarily used to demonstrate reflux.

qs.q: A 4-year-old girl is diagnosed with primary vesicoureteric reflux after a second episode of febrile urinary tract infection. Which factor is most strongly associated with the subsequent development of reflux nephropathy in pediatric patients?
o: Younger age at the time of the initial presentation
Male sex and recurrent asymptomatic bacteriuria
Presence of a duplicated renal collecting system
qs.e: Younger age at diagnosis and recurrent infections are major risk factors for renal scarring in reflux nephropathy. Proteinuria and duplication are less direct predictors of progressive parenchymal damage than age and infection frequency.
